Gini importance is a measure of how much a feature contributes to the homogeneity of the nodes and leaves in the decision tree. It is calculated as the weighted average of the Gini impurity decrease for each feature, where the weights are the proportion of samples that reach each node. The Gini impurity is a measure of how often a randomly chosen element from a set would be incorrectly labeled if it were randomly labeled according to the distribution of labels in the set.

The feature with the highest Gini importance is the one that contributes the most to the homogeneity of the nodes and leaves in the decision tree, and therefore is considered the most important feature.
